comments.quote_zh: 去看 Robert Whyte 的报告。
comments.text_zh: 去看 Robert Whyte 的报告。[VIDEO] 基本问题都已经解决了，科学问题也已经解决了。托卡马克已经实现过净聚变功率。已经成功的 JET 和 ARC 之间的唯一区别，就是使用场强高 2.6 倍的磁体。按 B^4 的功率标度关系，你能得到大约 50 倍的功率，所以 ARC 会发出 500 MW 的功率，而 JET（记住，这是已经验证过的工程）发出的是 10 MW。所以毫无疑问，到这一步这只是一个工程问题。一台不需要维护的原型装置，可以完全像任何其他托卡马克那样造出来，只是换上 REBCO 磁体，你就能得到所需的聚变功率。要得到所需的电功率，再加上维护需求，你还需要 FLiBe 液态包层、可更换的环向段和一个热交换器，但同样，这些都是已知的工程问题，有已知的解决方案，就好比知道火箭着陆是可能的，但还得搞定栅格翼、隔热罩、着陆腿和制导软件。小尺度的聚变装置从 90 年代起就一直在验证等离子体物理。我们至今还没有聚变，纯粹是因为人们保守，死守着传统上"已知可行"的磁体，这就是为什么 ITER 是个庞大笨重的巨兽。正如 Whyte 博士所说，成本随 R 缩放，而仅仅通过换用不同的磁体，R 就能比 ITER 缩小 10 倍，所以 ARC 会发出与 ITER 相同的功率，但体积小得多、便宜得多。基础论文
comments.text: Watch Robert Whyte's presentation. [VIDEO] The basic problems have all been solved, the science has been solved too. Tokamaks have already made net fusion power. The only difference between JET, which already succeeded, and ARC, is using Magnets with 2.6x the field strength. The B^4 power scaling, gives you about 50x the power, so ARC will generate 500 MW of power whereas JET (remember, already proven engineering), generated 10MW. So without a doubt, this is just an engineering problem at this point. A prototype device that didn't have to be maintained, could be built exactly like any other Tokamak, just with REBCO magnets, and you'd have the required fusion power. To get the required electric power, and add in maintenance, you need to at the FliBe liquid blanket, replacable toroid sections, and a heat exchanger, but again, these are known engineering problems with known solutions, akin to knowing that landing a rocket is possible, but figuring out the grid fins, heat shield, landing legs, and guidance software. Fusion devices on a small scale have been proving the plasma physics since the 90s. We don't have fusion yet simply because of people being conservative and sticking with traditional "known to work" magnets, which is why ITER is a huge, hulking monstrosity. As Dr Whyte says, cost scales by R, R can be reduced by a factor of 10 from ITER simply by using different magnets, so ARC will produce the same power as ITER, but significantly smaller and cheaper. comments.text_zh: 真正的重磅在这里，来自 MIT：[视频]。显然最近超导体有了突破，可以在保持超导性的同时让电感线圈中通过显著更大的电流。这反过来又能产生强得多的磁场，从而把等离子体约束得更紧，也就带来更多聚变。采用这些新型超导体的标准托卡马克应该能输出大于输入的能量，并成为可行的能源来源。
comments.text: The real deal is here, from MIT: [VIDEO] Apparently there was a recent breakthrough in superconductors, which allows significantly more current in the inductor coils while still maintaining superconductivity. This in turn allows for much stronger magnetic fields, hence tighter confinement of the plasma and therefore more fusion. A standard tokamak with these new superconductors should produce more energy out than energy in, and be a viable source of energy.

comments.why_zh: 关于聚变功率增长的图表，以及为什么更好的磁体能改变成本
comments.quote_zh: 真正让人大开眼界的是 18:03 那张图
comments.text_zh: 真正让人大开眼界的是 18:03 那张图：“从 1970 到 1995 年，[聚变]功率和能量的增长速度远快于算力（Moore's Law）” [1]。Whyte 博士认为，磁约束聚变之所以停滞，是因为要获得更高的功率（和效率），我们需要更强的磁场。要获得更强的磁场，就需要更大的磁体。要支撑更大的磁体，就需要更大的结构。大磁体和大结构会吸收更多的磁通量和中子通量；这会提高维护频率、复杂度和成本。更好的超导体让我们无需更大的磁体就能获得更强的磁场。这就改变了成本函数。[1] [VIDEO]
comments.text: Eye opener is the chart at 18:03: "from 1970 to 1995, [fusion] power and energy increased much faster than computing power (Moore's Law)" [1]. Magnetic-confinement fusion stalled, according to Dr. Whyte, because to get more power (and efficiency) we need stronger fields. To get stronger fields we needed bigger magnets. To support bigger magnets one needs bigger structures. Big magnets and big structures will absorb more magnetic and neutron flux; that increases maintenance frequency, complexity and cost. Better superconductors let us get stronger fields without bigger magnets. That changes the cost function. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.text: I’ve been following them since they were giving promising lectures at MIT and I absolutely think they have the most solid approach! comments.text: Sadly, that joke is at least 30 years old too. There are lots of companies in the game now. Tri Alpha Energy, General Fusion, Lockheed Martin and there are quite a few more. Humanity is going to get usable energy generated from fusion.

comments.author: matt2000
comments.story_title: United States should prepare to build a prototype fusion power plant, panel says
comments.why_zh: 更多关于让聚变项目更小更便宜的内容
comments.quote_zh: 更多内容见这里
comments.text_zh: 我非常反感聚变研究周围常见的那套话术。它往往不公平地把讨论框定在一项一旦实现就会改变世界的技术上。比如这篇文章里说："备受争议的 ITER 项目，一座极其昂贵的聚变反应堆……"毫无疑问这是个昂贵的项目，总成本估计约 200 亿美元（[LINK]）。但就可能的回报而言，甚至与其他项目相比，它其实很便宜。比如波士顿的"大开挖"（Big Dig）花了 240 亿美元：[LINK]。你更想要哪个？一条 1.5 米的隧道，还是一个能改变人类文明未来的能源？我在这里有点不公平，因为 Big Dig 本身就是管理不善和成本超支的典型案例，但作为一个社会，我们应该愿意把大量资源投入到能改变世界的研究上，而不是比如花 225 亿美元造三艘新船：[LINK]。话虽如此，往前走的路大概是想办法让聚变相关项目的规模和成本都变小。这样就能多个方案并行推进，而不用背负那么多组织和政府层面的开销。更多内容见这里：[VIDEO]
comments.text: I strongly object to the language that's commonly used around fusion research. Much of it unfairly frames the discussion around what would be a world-changing technology if realized. For example, in this article: "the controversial ITER project, a hugely expensive fusion reactor..." There is no doubt this is an expensive project, estimated at ~$20B total cost ( [LINK] ) However, in terms of possible upsides or even compared to other projects it's _cheap_. Boston's "Big Dig" was $24B for example: [LINK] Which would you rather have? A 1.5m tunnel, or an energy source that would change the future of human civilization? I am being somewhat unfair here since the Big Dig was a case study of mismanagement and cost overruns, but as a society we should be willing to spend significant resources on world changing research instead of say $22.5B on three new boats: [LINK] All that being said, the way forward is probably to figure out ways to make fusion related projects smaller in scale and cost. Then multiple attempts can proceed in parallel without all the organizational and governmental overhead. More on that here: [VIDEO]
